title: Canteen
summary: Scene 9. Supper in the Long Hall. Taka claims the six as his table, then Vetch reads the evening's orders and gives Section Nine the storm drains.
goal: Taka has claimed the six as his table, and Vetch has given Section Nine tonight's job in front of the hall.
howToPlay: Loud and warm, then one flat turn. Let them eat and talk; bring Vetch in when the talk slows. **After his order, Taka gets the last word.**

intro.where: The Long Hall, the base's canteen, at the evening sitting.
intro.readAloud: You hear the Long Hall before you see it: several hundred candidates at long tables, all talking at once about the same day. Every table already seems to belong to somebody. Behind the serving line, a radio is playing an evening phone-in that nobody is listening to.
intro.landmark: The serving line, with the radio on a shelf behind it.

carriesIn.then: Half the hall has heard. People grin at Section Nine on the way past, and Taka already knows.
The hall has heard about the bubble. Somebody asks how it's going.

position.note: Section Nine at one table near the serving line.

cast.role: A candidate a year ahead, who takes them under his wing.

brief.wants: Six new faces at his table tonight, before anyone else claims them.
brief.opensWith: Two chairs dragged over before anyone asks him to sit: "Budge up. Properly. There's six of you and I'm not sitting on the end like a coat."

willDiscuss.note: He asks first, and actually listens: "No, properly from."
"Forms. Then forms about the forms. Then they let you near a machine."
"Did he send you for the bubble? He sends everyone for the bubble."
"They play that every night. Somebody's always angry about something. Pickles?"

willNotDiscuss.why: He just won't, and it costs him nothing: "Nah. Have you tried the pickles?"

coercible.how: Ask him properly, after the order. He won't volunteer it, and he won't lie.

voice.register: Loud, warm and quick, with a real question in every third sentence. Goes quiet for a moment when something real comes up.
samples: "First day? Then you've had the forms. Mother's maiden name, twice. Everybody laughs at it. Nobody knows why."
"Right. Who's from furthest away? Go on."

brief.statblock: Proposed: level 2, a candidate, can fight. Perception DC 18, Will DC 18, Deception DC 17.

cast.role: Duty officer tonight, reading the evening's orders.

brief.wants: To watch Section Nine get the worst job on the list, from him, in front of everyone.
brief.opensWith: Nothing to the six. He reads the hall its orders and looks up only for theirs.

willDiscuss.note: He reads it again, word for word, once. Not a third time.

willNotDiscuss.why: "I don't know what you're referring to."
"Sections are assigned work. That is what a section is."

voice.register: Clipped and procedural. Reads orders like a shopping list. Never wrong in his own account.
samples: "Section Nine." He looks up. "Yes, you. There's only one of you."

brief.statblock: Proposed: level 3, an officer, non-combat. Perception DC 19, Will DC 19, Deception DC 19. Striking him ends in a hearing, not a fight.

cast.role: A pilot-track candidate at the next table.

brief.wants: Everyone to know his section got harbour patrol.
brief.opensWith: "Which track are you on?" before anyone's name.

voice.register: Confident and a little competitive, not unkind.
samples: "Section Nine? Rough. We got harbour patrol."

beats.text: Let them find a table and talk. Read the radio once, under the noise.
beats.readAloud: On the radio, a father is trying hard not to shout. His daughter is seventeen, she's being held without charge, and nobody will tell him where.
beats.note:
Plant: Nobody in the hall reacts to the radio. Say nothing more about it.
Secret: She is Shinobu Kudo, and he is her father. She comes back into the story much later.

beats.text: Taka <trig id="taka-arrives"/> arrives with two chairs, claims the six as his table, and asks each of them where they're properly from.
beats.direction: Full warmth: he asks about each of them and listens. Warm by including them, never by labelling them.

beats.text: Vetch <trig id="section-officer-arrives"/> reads the evening's orders to the hall. Section Nine's is last. <trig id="give-drains"/>
beats.readAloud: "Section Four: harbour patrol, east gate. Section Six: survey with Structural, Hangar Two." He looks up for the first time. "Section Nine: storm drain clearance under the old town. Dock C at twenty-one hundred. Waders from the night lockup."
beats.direction: No choice and no appeal: he answers any argument by reading the order again, once, and goes.
beats.note:
If someone refuses outright: "Noted." He writes it down, slowly. "The Deputy Director's office, twenty-one hundred, instead of Dock C."
If someone missed supper: A runner finds them with a chit: the same order, word for word.
Secret: He gave them the drains for the vial, or, if they came back empty-handed, for the laugh. He'll never say so.

beats.text: If anyone watches Vetch rather than listening to him, offer the check.
The hall goes back to its supper. The next table gloats about harbour patrol, and Taka gets the last word. <trig id="drains-wear-them"/>
beats.readAloud: "Storm drains." Taka is quiet for a moment, which is new. "Wear the waders. Trust me."
beats.note: If anyone answers the next table's "Which track are you on?": "No track? Huh. Never seen that." He means nothing by it.

beats.text: If anyone asks Taka properly what's down there, offer the check.

when.condition: someone asks Taka about the drains

outro.endsWhen: Taka has had the last word.

tracks.why: If Taka's table, or the order, pulled the six together.

transition.line: Dock C at twenty-one hundred, with waders from the night lockup.

outro.onwards: The Walk Down, to the night lockup and Dock C.
writeDown: Who took to Taka, and who he took to.
Anything Taka told them about the drains.

temptations.text: Taka knows everyone on this island, and he's dying to be asked something.

notes: Taka's warmth is inclusion, never nicknames. The pilot-track candidate is the Young One: play him as an ordinary, slightly smug classmate, nothing more.
